study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative Modeling of Brain Morphometry in Clinical High Risk for Psychosis

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Quantify individual-level deviations from normative neuroanatomical variation in CHR-P and evaluate overlap with healthy variation and associations with positive symptoms, cognition, and conversion to psychosis.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (87 datasets; ENIGMA Lifespan WG and collaborators)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The normative models were trained on a pooled multi-site healthy reference sample via CentileBrain.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: "...in a sample of 37,407 healthy individuals ... pooled from 81 datasets."; "Sex-specific normative models ... CentileBrain ... developed using data from an independent multisite sample of 37 407 healthy individuals (53.3% female; aged 3-90 years)."

rci2_hc_n.reason: The manuscript explicitly states that normative models were developed using data from 37,407 healthy individuals. This is the reference cohort for normative modeling, distinct from the 1237 healthy individuals in the ENIGMA CHR-P Working Group who were used to test/validate the models.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: the normative models for each regional measure in the framework were developed using data from an independent multisite sample of 37 407 healthy individuals (53.3% female; aged 3-90 years)
rci2_hc_n.location: Haas2024.pdf.md: Methods / Normative Modeling of Brain Morphometry, L70

rci3_hc_age.answer: Phase: Uninvestigated | mean: 39.88 | sd: 23.47 | median: NR | iqr: NR | min: 3 | max: 90

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: Structural MRI T1-weighted scans used at each site.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: "...participants underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) to obtain T1-weighted scans."

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: ComBat-GAM harmonization during normative model training; sensitivity analyses included site as random effect in linear mixed-effects models; leave-one-site-out checks reported.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: "...site harmonization (ComBat-GAM [combatting batch effects-generalized additive model])"; "...including site as a random effect in linear mixed-effects models (eTable 15)..."; "leave-one-site-out analysis (eFigure 11)"

nm1_model_origin.detail: CentileBrain lifespan normative models trained via MFPR on 37,407 healthy participants (81 datasets), with ComBat-GAM harmonization and covariates (ICV for SV, mean CT for CT, mean SA for SA).
nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: "...MFPR ... in a sample of 37,407 healthy individuals ... pooled from 81 datasets ... site harmonization (ComBat-GAM) and inclusion of intracranial volume, mean CT, and mean SA..."

caa1_clinical_dataset.answer: ENIGMA Clinical High Risk for Psychosis Working Group
caa1_clinical_dataset.reason: This is the explicitly named dataset used for the clinical group (CHR-P) and the matched healthy comparison group.
caa1_clinical_dataset.supporting_text: Thestudysamplewasderivedfromthepooleddatasetof individuals with CHR-P and healthy individuals held by the ENIGMA CHR-P Working Group (eMethods and eTable 1 in Supplement1).

caa2_diseases_studied.answer: Clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P); conversion to psychotic disorder
caa2_diseases_studied.reason: Target population and conversion subgroup stated.
caa2_diseases_studied.supporting_text: Title and methods refer to CHR-P; conversion status analyses reported.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Regional deviations largely nested within healthy range; small minority show extreme deviations; higher infranormal ADS in CHR-P; limited associations with symptoms; converters show more infranormal temporal deviations.
